history: I cleaned his wounds, applied a Trauma Dressing and secured both restraints. Daniel remained lucid. The dressing bought time; it did not cure him.
Daniel warned me that the corridor purge handle opens three exterior windows, and that spare patrol equipment was left behind the ward entry rather than on the bedside shelves.
I left Daniel alive and untreated. The right wrist restraint was fraying. I could still return with a Trauma Dressing while he remained lucid.
I returned after leaving him untreated. Daniel no longer recognized me. His right restraint had snapped; his left wrist still held him on the bed.
I secured Daniel’s broken restraint. Reaching inside his grasp cost me 9 health. The repaired strap keeps him away from the doorway; he cannot follow me.
I ended Daniel’s life while he could still understand me with the utility knife. I covered him with the bed sheet. This cannot be undone.
I ended Daniel’s life while he could still understand me with one firearm round. I covered him with the bed sheet. This cannot be undone.

kessler.record:
DR. ADRIAN KESSLER / THEATRE OBSERVATION

His eyes briefly find mine. “You were awake the first time.” The recognition breaks into a wet cough. A spasm takes his legs, and he collapses against the tiles, one hand still clawing at the wall.

I chose to call his name. The encounter is over; his infected aftermath remains in the theatre.

DR. ADRIAN KESSLER / THEATRE OBSERVATION

Kessler turns before I can touch his shoulder. His hand rakes my arm. I recoil as a convulsion folds him against the wall; dark veins tighten along his neck. His grasp cost me 6 health.

I chose to approach him. The encounter is over; his infected aftermath remains in the theatre.

DR. ADRIAN KESSLER / THEATRE OBSERVATION

I keep watching. The impacts lose their rhythm. Dark veins spread along his jaw; his teeth work against an empty mouth. His legs finally buckle, but the twitching does not stop.

I chose to watch from the doorway. The encounter is over; his infected aftermath remains in the theatre.

DR. ADRIAN KESSLER / THEATRE OBSERVATION

I back out of reach. Two final impacts come from the alcove, then a scraping collapse. From the doorway I can still see his jaw working and the dark veins above his collar.

I chose to back away. The encounter is over; his infected aftermath remains in the theatre.
